archetypes.name: plan-coherence
archetypes.rationale: The plan has at least three internal contradictions that would cause an implementer to make wrong choices: the require_key add-vs-don't-add flip between the UPDATED section and the Failure modes section, the 'DECISION_3 = 7 flags only' label while the plan body enumerates 8 flags including --force-init-state, and the '38-key heredoc' claim against a SKILL.md list that enumerates 39 keys. None of the static personas hunt intra-plan contradictions; they hunt plan-vs-code divergences.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the full plan and find every place where two sections give conflicting instructions for the same decision point. Flag each contradiction with both the conflicting statements quoted verbatim and the specific plan section each appears in. Pay particular attention to: (1) whether the three new keys (BAIL_FAILURE_DETAIL_LOG, NO_LOGS_COMMIT, IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR) should or should not be added to the require_key enumeration — the plan states both outcomes in different sections; (2) whether DECISION_3 is accurately labeled '7 caller-varying flags only' given that --force-init-state is also introduced as a new flag; (3) whether the stated key count ('38-key heredoc') matches the actual count in the referenced SKILL.md lines. Cross-check the plan's DECISION_2 narrative ('one ordered key-list constant shared by write_initial_state and require_key') against the file-modification section, which shows no such constant being created. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: state-key-enumeration
archetypes.rationale: The plan's core claim is that adding three printf lines to write_initial_state() produces byte-for-byte parity with the orchestrator's heredoc. Verifying that claim requires a precise diff of the current write_initial_state() key set, the SKILL.md documented key set, and the require_key enumeration — none of which the static personas enumerate exhaustively from file evidence.
archetypes.prompt_body:
Read scripts/ship-pr.sh write_initial_state() (around line 239) and count the exact set of keys it currently emits. Read the require_key loop (around line 2437) and list which keys are required. Read skills/implement/SKILL.md lines 1550-1559 and list the documented key set. Produce a three-column diff: keys in write_initial_state, keys in require_key, keys in SKILL.md. Identify any key present in one list but absent from another that the plan does not explicitly address. Check whether the plan correctly claims the three new keys (BAIL_FAILURE_DETAIL_LOG, NO_LOGS_COMMIT, IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR) are the only ones missing from write_initial_state(), or whether additional keys are missing. Verify that BAIL_REASON (currently written by write_initial_state at the printf 'BAIL_REASON=%s
' line) is distinct from BAIL_FAILURE_DETAIL_LOG and that the plan does not conflate them. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-integration
archetypes.rationale: The plan proposes four test cases that must run under the existing write_subject/write_stubs scaffolding and must never source the state file. The cases involve forcing ship-pr.sh to write a state file and then exit in an inspectable way — but ship-pr.sh's main loop after write_initial_state() runs many stubs and expects a live git repo. Whether the cases can reach an assertable exit point using the current stubs, and whether the CR/LF case can be expressed portably in Bash 3.2, are questions only harness-level reading can answer.
archetypes.prompt_body:
Read scripts/test-ship-pr.sh from the top to understand write_subject(), write_stubs(), the section dispatch mechanism, and which make targets each section maps to. Determine whether the existing stub set (run-relevant-checks-captured.sh, implement-finalize.sh, etc.) would allow a fresh ship-pr.sh invocation — one that hits write_initial_state() then exits — to reach exit 0 or another predictable exit code without additional stubs. Check whether the plan's proposed grep-based state-file assertions ('grep ^BRANCH_NAME= | cut -d= -f2-') would correctly extract multi-character values containing equals signs, given the current printf '%s
' format in write_initial_state(). Verify that the CR/LF rejection test using printf '\r' inside a Bash 3.2 case pattern is correctly expressed (Bash 3.2 supports ANSI-C quoting $'\r' in patterns). Check whether the plan's claim that new cases run under 'make test-ship-pr-state' is consistent with the section= dispatch logic in the harness. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
